standard_prerequisites.use: Writes the dense open U as a finite union of distinguished opens D(f_i), which is what makes the injectivity of A -> product of the localisations available.

standard_prerequisites.name: Finiteness of presentation at a point for a flat finite type module, and openness of flatness
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter flat.tex, label lemma-finite-type-flat-at-point-local (proof line 2970); Algebra, label algebra-theorem-openness-flatness (proof line 2981)
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives that the localisation of the module at the chosen prime is finitely presented over the local ring and, after constructing a model that agrees with it there, that the model is flat over the base on a neighbourhood of the point.

standard_prerequisites.name: A local presentation argument, and the local nature of finite presentation
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, labels algebra-lemma-cover (proof line 2996) and algebra-lemma-extension (used in the same section)
standard_prerequisites.use: The cover lemma lets a local finite presentation statement be concluded globally, which is how the proof finishes from the affine neighbourhood found at the chosen point.

core_obligations: Reduce to affine X and S and write the module as the sheaf of a finite B-module N; write the dense open U as a finite union of principal opens D(f_i) of A, so that A -> product of A_{f_i} is injective (proof lines 2960-2967).

At a prime q of B over a prime p of A, use finiteness of presentation at the point to build a finitely presented model N' of the localisation: choose a surjection from a free module onto N, pick finitely many elements of its kernel to define N' as the quotient, and choose them so that N' localised at each f_i agrees with N and N' localised at q agrees with N (proof lines 2968-2979).

Conclude that N is finitely presented: the model is flat over A at q by construction, so by openness of flatness it becomes flat after inverting some g outside q; the commutative square comparing N'_g with N_g over the products of the localisations of the model and of N has an isomorphic bottom arrow by construction and an injective left arrow because A -> product A_{f_i} is injective and the model is flat, hence the top arrow is an isomorphism, so N_g is finitely presented and the cover lemma finishes (proof lines 2979-2996).
proof_roadmap: Go affine and express the dense open by finitely many principal opens (proof lines 2960-2967).
Build a finitely presented model of the module that agrees with it on the dense open and at the chosen point (proof lines 2968-2979).
Use flatness, the injective comparison square and the cover lemma to conclude finite presentation (proof lines 2979-2996).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a finite type module which is flat over the base and finitely presented over a retrocompact scheme theoretically dense open is finitely presented on the nose (statement lines 2942-2958, tag 081N). The proof is a genuine construction: after going affine and expressing the dense open by finitely many principal opens, it builds a finitely presented model of the module that agrees with it on those opens and at a chosen prime, uses openness of flatness to make the model flat on a neighbourhood, and then reads off from an injective comparison square that the module itself becomes finitely presented there. The model construction and the comparison square are the substance, so the claim is H2.
